question: On Saturday 2 August, Türkiye published a map of two so-called ‘marine parks’ which extend beyond Turkish territorial waters, west of Imbros and Tenedos between the Greek islands of Samothrace and Lemnos, and north east of Rhodes, surrounding Kastellorizo, in violation of the international law of the sea (UNCLOS), which recognises full rights for island territories irrespective of size or proximity to other mainland coasts.

The areas in which Türkiye is attempting to impose marine parks in violation of international law include areas of potential Greek continental shelf and EEZ and territorial waters, which, on the basis of UNCLOS, are the rights of the Greek islands of the Aegean.

The map was submitted to the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of UNESCO without prior consultation, with the obvious aim of attempting to create a fait accompli and continue the provocations against Greece. Such unilateral and legally unfounded practices affect the sovereign rights of a Member State and undermine stability in the Eastern Mediterranean and the Aegean. In view of this: 1.
What measures does the Commission intend to take to provide practical support to Greece against Türkiye's unilateral actions?

As the MSPglobal initiative on maritime spatial planning, which operates within the framework of the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of UNESCO, is cofinanced by DG MARE, what will the Commission do to prevent the publication of a map that blatantly violates the sovereign rights of a Member State?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.10.2025) The EU has a strategic interest in a stable and secure environment in the Eastern Mediterranean and has called on Türkiye to fully respect international law, to de-escalate tensions in the interest of regional stability in the Eastern Mediterranean, and to promote good-neighbourly relations in a sustainable way1.

In the same context, the EU remains determined to use, if need be, the instruments and options at its disposal to defend its interests and those of its Member States. The EU has noted the recent improvements in relations between Greece and Türkiye in the expectation that they will be sustainable2. To this respect, Greece and Türkiye have activated multiple work strands.

The EU has also made clear that Türkiye must respect the sovereignty, and territorial integrity of all Member States, as well as all their sovereign rights and continues to expect Türkiye to unequivocally commit to the peaceful settlement of disputes, having recourse, if necessary, to the International Court of Justice3.

The Commission does not have information about submission of the Türkiye’s declaration of marine parks to the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). Such map is not published anywhere on the Maritime Spatial Planning Global (MSPglobal) site.

MSPglobal country profile for Türkiye does not display any map and contains a disclaimer, that ‘the information in this country profile does not imply the expression of any opinion whatsoever on the part of UNESCO concerning the legal status of any country, territory, city or area or its authorities, or concerning the delimitation of its frontiers or boundaries.
Links to other sites are provided for information only’.
